summary: I withdrew from the batch-size family (4 of 6 agents had claimed it) and mapped model shape under the 300s budget. Shallow+wide won: on a5's window-256 + a3's 2**18-batch base, DEPTH=6 / ASPECT_RATIO=106 (6 layers, dim 640, 5 heads of 128) gave val_bpb 0.982903 vs 0.987049, a two-constant change that improved both throughput (MFU 38->40%, 484M tokens) and loss-per-token. The shape curve at 2**18 batch is d12/384 0.999969 > d8/512 0.987049 > d6/640 0.982903 < d5/768 0.984286, and a 3x MLP at d6/640 (0.987336) fixes the other side, so the optimum is ~30M matrix params spent as few wide layers with a 4x MLP. What did not work: scaling the model up (d10/640 at 2**19, 1.002227), deeper+narrower at constant params, and - importantly - stacking a1's prefetch loader + a0's warmdown 0.8 onto my shape (0.983617, no gain), because the wide-shallow model is GPU-bound and the CPU-loader win measured at d8/512 evaporates. Next I would re-tune LR, warmdown and batch size directly on d6/640 (peak LR likely wants raising at dim 640) and probe d7/640 and GQA, rather than chase more layers.
